Definition: from G2596 and G3539; to observe fully:--behold, consider, discover, perceive.
BiblicalUsage: To consider is to observe fully, and we are told to consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, to consider one another to provoke unto love and good works, to consider the lilies and the ravens, and to see the man who beholds his face in a glass and goes away forgetting what he looked like. The word asks for a long look, not a glance, and what you look at longest shapes what you become.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe consideration is the discipline behind devotion, because you become like what you keep looking at. I hold that if I consider Christ first, everything else falls into its right place.
